family: The single total polynomial-time language defined in proof.md: f_0=0. For n>=1 choose the least positive integer s with s^5>=4*n^3 and the least prime k>s; return 0 if k>=n. Otherwise the last k input bits encode a monic degree-k binary polynomial h and the first N=n-k bits are data. In F_2[Z]/(h), pad the data into r=ceil(N/k) blocks X_j, put t=ceil(sqrt(r)) and u_j=r+1-j, and output the constant coefficient of the degree-t elementary symmetric sum on X_j^(2^u_j-1). This ring evaluator is defined even for reducible h. Its empty-witness verifier accepts exactly its yes inputs.
theorem: For this one fixed total uniform polynomial-time family, hence in NP with witness bound zero, there exists an integer n_0 such that for every integer actual input length n>=n_0, C_B2(f_n)>=4*n-(359/25)*n^(4/5) in the full Li–Yang B2 model, and hence liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=4.
